2.Mr.A.Baskaran, learned Additional Government Pleader takes notice for the respondents 1 to 3.
By consent of both parties, the Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal.

3.It is the case of the Petitioner that the second respondent issued a notification for acquiring lands of the Petitioner situated in S.Nos.169/2B1, 169/2B2, 104/2A, 171/2B, 171/5A,172/1A of Aarchampatti, R.T.Mahal Village and Post, Kulithalai Taluk, Karur District for the project called Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundaru Link Canal Project.

After considering the representation of the Petitioner regarding fixation of compensation for the acquired lands, the competent authority passed the impugned order on 29.11.2024 determining the compensation amount payable to the Petitioners.
Not satisfied with the same, the Petitioners have filed this Writ Petition.

4.If the Petitioners are not satisfied with the determination of compensation by the competent authority, it is for them to make an application under Section 64(2)(a) of the Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within six weeks from https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 10/06/2025 07:19:36 pm )
the date of the award.

entities.text: Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: When the Petitioners have got a remedy of seeking reference under Section 64 of the above-said Act, the writ Petition filed by the Petitioners cannot be entertained.

It is also pertinent to note that the Petitioners failed to implead the authority who passed the impugned order namely, the Special District Revenue Officer(Land Acquisition), Cauvery-Vaigai- Gundaru Link Canal Project, Karur District.

5.Therefore the Writ Petition is dismissed, with liberty to the Petitioners to seek reference under Section 64 of the Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Nagalakshmi vs The State Of Tamil Nadu on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6738713/
2 and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Nagalakshmi vs The State Of Tamil Nadu
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is made clear the Petitioners are entitled to exclude the time taken by them in prosecuting the Writ Petition before this Court(ie.,03.04.2025 to date of receipt of this order), while calculating limitation for application under Section 64(2)(a) of Right To Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: No Costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
